decisions.reason: Having survived an initial review and remained a prominently presented core-adjacent camera, Product A is likely performing at or above aspiration levels, so a large R&D-intensive firm with some slack would keep it.

Product D still carries moderate risk because commercialization signals have been weaker, but its fit with the firm's miniaturized sensor trajectory and available organizational slack make retention more likely than withdrawal.

As a newly launched product line with dedicated presentation and very strong overlap with the firm's established radiation-tolerant imaging capabilities, Product E is likely to be given time to prove itself and kept.

Because Product F appears more niche and less central to the firm's stated strategic direction while showing only tentative market presentation, management would likely judge its early results below aspiration and reallocate resources elsewhere.
